abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for hybrid quantum-classical computing architectures that fundamentally reimagines computational problem-solving paradigms. Traditional computing systems face inherent limitations when addressing optimization problems in large-scale networks, communications, and signal processing domains. We propose a hierarchical quantum error mitigation scheme that enables seamless integration of quantum computing modules with classical infrastructure. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that our approach achieves exponential speedup for specific NP-hard problems while maintaining classical compatibility. We introduce a unified mathematical model that characterizes the quantum advantage boundaries through rigorous complexity-theoretic arguments. The framework addresses fundamental challenges in quantum error correction by proposing adaptive threshold techniques that scale with qubit quality. Our contribution establishes theoretical foundations for next-generation computing architectures that transcend the von Neumann bottleneck. Simulation results validate the theoretical predictions across multiple problem instances from telecommunications and control theory domains. This paradigm shift enables practical quantum advantage in near-term devices with limited coherence times. The implications extend to emerging technologies including cryptographic protocols, machine learning acceleration, and large-scale system optimization. This work opens new research directions at the intersection of quantum physics, computer engineering, and information theory.

This paper develops an enhanced theoretical analysis of sparse signal recovery algorithms that substantially improves upon existing compressed sensing methods for communication systems. Prior approaches suffer from suboptimal recovery guarantees when handling correlated measurement matrices commonly encountered in broadband telecommunications. We propose a weighted L1 optimization framework with theoretically proven guarantees under restricted isometry property conditions. The analysis establishes tighter bounds on sample complexity by exploiting the inherent structure of wireless channel matrices. Our main result demonstrates that the proposed method achieves O(k log n) sampling complexity with significantly reduced coherence requirements compared to state-of-the-art approaches. We further provide convergence analysis for the associated proximal gradient algorithm with linear convergence rates. The theoretical contributions include novel concentration inequalities for random matrices with correlated entries and applications to massive MIMO channel estimation. Extensive numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings across various signal processing scenarios. The proposed framework demonstrates up to 40% improvement in reconstruction accuracy while reducing computational complexity by an order of magnitude. This work provides rigorous mathematical foundations for practical implementation in next-generation wireless systems, contributing to the advancement of signal processing theory and its applications in telecommunications infrastructure.

We present a comprehensive system architecture for intelligent edge computing in IoT networks that fundamentally transforms how distributed sensing and actuation are coordinated. Conventional cloud-centric approaches introduce unacceptable latency for time-critical applications in healthcare monitoring, autonomous robotics, and industrial control. Our proposed EdgeMind framework introduces a hierarchical intelligence distribution mechanism where lightweight neural processing units are embedded at network edge nodes. The system design incorporates novel attention-based task allocation protocols that dynamically distribute computational workloads based on real-time resource availability and task criticality. We implement a prototype deployment across heterogeneous hardware platforms including ARM-based microcontrollers, FPGA accelerators, and specialized AI chips. The architecture supports seamless offloading decisions through learned prediction models that minimize energy consumption while meeting quality-of-service requirements. Experimental evaluation demonstrates 85% reduction in end-to-end latency compared to cloud-only approaches while achieving 60% energy savings through intelligent workload distribution. The system maintains robust performance under varying network conditions and supports graceful degradation when connectivity is compromised. This paradigm shift enables real-time AI capabilities for smart systems operating in bandwidth-constrained environments. The design principles are applicable across healthcare, transportation, and smart city infrastructure domains.

This paper presents an enhanced robotic manipulation system that significantly advances dexterous grasping capabilities through novel integration of multimodal sensing and deep reinforcement learning. Existing approaches struggle with the sim-to-real transfer gap when deploying learned policies on physical robots handling novel objects. We introduce a domain-adaptive control architecture featuring a hierarchical policy structure with task-agnostic skill embeddings. The system incorporates tactile sensing arrays and visual feedback with novel fusion mechanisms that capture contact dynamics during manipulation tasks. Our design employs curriculum-based training with progressive complexity increases, enabling efficient learning on limited demonstration data. We develop a real-time grasp planning module that achieves 94% success rate on novel objects, representing substantial improvement over baseline methods. The complete system operates at 30Hz control frequency with end-to-end latency under 15ms, meeting requirements for responsive robotic control. Extensive evaluation across 200 distinct objects demonstrates robust generalization capabilities. The architecture incorporates safety-critical shutdown mechanisms compliant with industrial robotics standards. We provide detailed implementation guidelines and open-source software components for replication. This work advances the state-of-the-art in autonomous robotics by bridging the gap between simulation and physical deployment, with clear implications for manufacturing automation and collaborative human-robot workspaces.
